question: Which human–AI scoring disagreements need review?
data: Synthetic paired human and AI ordinal scores with uncertainty values.
method: Calculate agreement and quadratic kappa; route large disagreements or uncertain scores to review.
interpretation: Agreement is not accuracy against a gold standard. Quadratic kappa discounts near misses but depends on score marginals; simulated uncertainty is not calibrated real-world uncertainty.
status: SYNTHETIC / RULE-BASED PROTOTYPE | no educational validity claim
table_title: Selected recorded values (units and context shown)
evidence_note: See CALCULATIONS.md for data status, execution scope and interpretation.
finding: This prototype compares synthetic human and AI assessment scores and produces a transparent review queue. It reports exact agreement, within-one agreement, quadratic kappa, and the proportion sent for review, using explicit disagreement and uncertainty thresholds. These outputs test the routing logic; they do not establish that an AI assessor is correct or that the thresholds are appropriate for real students.
